Visit note | 2025-01-06 09:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Masud Patwary, 61, male. The patient presents complaining of neck tightness and a band-like pressure around his head, which he attributes to spending long hours at a screen. He mentions that these symptoms began after a stressful house move to Sylhet. He works as a restaurant cook. He has a known history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies any visual changes, nausea, or vomiting. On examination: pain score 4/10, BP 128/75 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 66 kg. Neurological exam is unremarkable with normal cranial nerves and no focal deficits. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-01-06 11:30 AM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Farzana Karim, 27, female. The patient presents to the clinic complaining of thick nasal discharge for over ten days, pressure over the cheeks and forehead, and a blocked nose. She describes the discharge as yellowish-green, persistent, and difficult to clear. She works as an office cleaner and notes that these nasal symptoms first began after diving at a pool in Dhanmondi about two weeks ago. She has a significant comorbidity of Type 2 diabetes mellitus, which is currently managed with oral medications. She reports a dull, throbbing headache that worsens when she bends forward or lies down. She denies any high-grade fever, double vision, swelling around the eyes, facial numbness, or stiffness in her neck. On physical examination: temperature 100.5°F, BP 132/76 mmHg, pulse 97 bpm, weight 62 kg. There is marked tenderness on palpation over both the maxillary and frontal sinus areas. Anterior rhinoscopy shows severely congested and erythematous nasal mucosa with thick, purulent discharge visible in the middle meatus. The oral cavity shows some post-nasal drip on the posterior pharyngeal wall, but no tonsillar hypertrophy or exudate is present. Otoscopy reveals normal tympanic membranes bilaterally with no fluid or retraction. There is no cervical lymphadenopathy. Neurological examination of the cranial nerves is completely normal, and there is no signs of any meningeal irritation. Assessment: Acute sinusitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was counselled on the nature of her sinus infection and how her diabetes might affect healing. She was advised to use steam inhalation twice daily to help clear the nasal passages and to drink warm fluids frequently to stay hydrated. She was instructed to avoid diving or swimming until she is fully recovered. She was also advised to monitor her blood sugar levels regularly during this illness and adjust her diet as needed. She should return immediately if she notices any warning signs such as vision changes, severe headache, high fever, or facial swelling. Follow-up in 10 days.
